# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 10 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 10 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_010_page_001.jpg

---

**10:1** It was Wisdom who watched over the father of the world — the one who was formed first, created alone — and rescued him from his own mistake,

**10:2** giving him the capacity to rule over everything.

**10:3** But when a man who had turned away from Wisdom acted in furious anger, he destroyed himself through the rage of murder — his own brother's blood on his hands.

**10:4** And when that sin brought a flood upon the earth, Wisdom rescued the world again — she guided a righteous man to safety through a few planks of wood.

**10:5** Again, when the nations were turning against one another in sinful conspiracy and collapsing into chaos, she singled out a righteous man and kept him untarnished before God — even when everything within him cried out to spare his son.

**10:6** When destruction rained down on five cities and the ungodly perished, Wisdom saved a righteous man — he escaped just in time.

**10:7** The evidence of that judgment is still there for anyone who looks: a land of desolation still smoking, trees that bear fruit but fruit that never ripens, and a standing pillar of salt — a permanent monument to a woman who refused to trust and could not let go.

**10:8** Because they turned their back on Wisdom, they suffered more than ignorance of the good; they left behind for the living a reminder of their foolishness so loud that their stumbling could never be forgotten.

**10:9** But Wisdom rescued those who served her from every trouble they faced.

**10:10** A righteous man fled his brother's rage, and Wisdom showed him the straight road. She revealed to him the kingdom of God and gave him insight into sacred things. She made his work succeed and multiplied the results of all his labor.

**10:11** When greedy men tried to crush him and cheat him, she stepped in and made him prosper.

**10:12** She shielded him from his enemies, kept him from those who set traps for him, and oversaw a brutal contest for him — so that he could discover firsthand that devotion to God is stronger than anything.

**10:13** When a righteous man was sold into slavery, Wisdom did not abandon him; she kept him from sin itself.

**10:14** She went down into the pit with him; she did not leave him in chains. In the end, she brought him a scepter and a kingdom — authority over the very people who had ruled over him. She exposed the lies of those who had slandered him and gave him glory that would never fade.

**10:15** She delivered a holy people — a blameless community — out of the hands of a nation that oppressed them.

**10:16** She entered the soul of a servant of the Lord and enabled him to stand before fearsome kings with wonders and signs.

**10:17** She paid the holy ones back for everything they had labored and suffered. She led them on an extraordinary road and became their shade by day and their guiding fire of stars by night.

**10:18** She carried them through the Red Sea and brought them safely through great waters.

**10:19** Their enemies she swallowed up — cast them out from the deep abyss.

**10:20** So the righteous plundered those who had oppressed them. They sang to you, Lord, praising your holy name, and with one voice they celebrated the hand that had fought for them —

**10:21** for it was Wisdom who opened the mouths of those who had been silent, and gave clear speech to those too young to form words.
